[Pedagogy review · High priority · missing-prerequisite · pf-b45bea7186]
Recovering length ratios from area or volume ratios is required without teaching the inverse relationship.
Before p6-q3c-node add: 'To recover a length ratio from an area ratio, take square roots of both terms. Areas 8 cm² and 18 cm² have ratio 4:9, so corresponding lengths have ratio √4:√9 = 2:3. A length of 6 cm on the smaller figure corresponds to 6 × 3/2 = 9 cm.' Before p12-q12-root add: 'To recover a length ratio from a volume ratio, take cube roots of both terms. Volume ratio 8:27 gives length ratio ∛8:∛27 = 2:3, then area ratio 2²:3² = 4:9.'
Also affects: p6-q3d-node, p7-q6, p12-row03, p12-row04, p12-row06, p12-row07, p12-row11, p13-q13-a

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-b0be692c63]
After p6-q4c-node, add part d: “The same park is redrawn using a scale of 2 cm = 10 m. What area does the playground occupy on the new diagram? Explain why.” Expected answer: 17.2 cm²; the diagram lengths double, so its area is multiplied by 2² = 4.

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-02c38b1a7d]
At p14-q17-response: After the existing question, add (b): “What fraction of the original ball’s surface area does one smaller ball have?” Expected answer: 1/25. Add (c): “How many times the original ball’s surface area is the combined surface area of all 125 smaller balls?” Expected answer: 5 times.
